$comment: Machine-readable catalog index for the explainer skill. The skill reads this to route a request to technique(s) + fidelity, then copies the matching template from assets/catalog/ and swaps its data (see assets/catalog/_data.template.js). Do not duplicate prose here that lives in references/*.md.
$comment_weak: '.when'/'.weak' are load-bearing for the post-build fit-check (references/quality-gate.md 'Fit-check'). '.when' = the question this technique answers; '.weak' = questions it does NOT. The fit-check quotes these verbatim to convict a suboptimal pick or spot a catalog gap. Keep them precise. New techniques enter first as candidates in references/catalog-gaps.md, then get promoted here on review.

ascii.what: Compact text diagram inline in chat. No file.
ascii.default_for: small subject, quick 'explain this', review-comment context

mermaid.default_for: medium subject, anything shipped into a doc/PR/wiki

html.what: Standalone interactive explainer using the locked shared design system.
html.default_for: large/complex subject, or when it must be viewed from multiple angles

families.value: where data comes from and goes

techniques.when: see where a change sits in the end-to-end flow; onboarding to a path
answer 'where does this value come from / go?' WITH the code at each point — including which side of the system boundary it was born on and which direction it crosses
techniques.weak: control flow; timing; the shape of the change itself; the box's whole surface at once (use io-boundary)
techniques.note: Supply BOUNDARY whenever the subject has a trust or ownership edge. Without it every value renders as a peer, which hides the only distinction that decides safety: an INPUT is not a peer of a LOCAL. With it, values sort by crossing (input, through, output, local) and each carries its class.

techniques.when: 'what enters this box, what leaves it, and which values are trusted?' — the whole surface on one screen; sizing a subsystem; finding the untrusted inputs and the external commitments
techniques.weak: the code at each point (pair with value-provenance or annotated-source); control flow; timing; how a flow composes ACROSS several systems / trust domains (use system-topology)
techniques.note: SIDE-CAR or primary. Systems-theory framing: a system is a box with a surface. Answers the question you must settle BEFORE reasoning about safety. Where value-provenance zooms into one value's code, this shows every crossing at once with no code. io-boundary is ONE box (its surface, all crossings at once); system-topology is the MULTI-SYSTEM node-link view (several boxes across trust domains, the dataflow between them).
techniques.classify_traps: A value read from input_data/path/query is INPUT even if it is later forwarded — 'also leaves' is a secondary fact, not its class. THROUGH is only for a value neither read nor acted on (a blind relay), which is rare. A value derived inside then sent onward is OUTPUT, not THROUGH. When unsure between INPUT and THROUGH, it is INPUT.

techniques.when: how systems compose ACROSS trust domains: what data rides each hop, whether it leaves us, the blast-radius of what is on the wire; following ONE value end-to-end through every system it touches; where a vendor / queue / datastore sits relative to our boundary
techniques.weak: line-by-line code; a single function's control flow; precise call timing (use runtime-step or swimlanes)
techniques.note: The systems-theory view, drawn as a NODE-LINK diagram over swimlanes (NOT a card grid). Each DOMAIN is a horizontal band (ours = blue, external = faded); dataflow runs left-to-right ACROSS the bands. ARROWS carry the data — the label on the arrow is what rides it; the full payload is click-to-reveal in an inspector, never dumped on the canvas (main fields shown, extra behind '+N more'). Care level shows as visual WEIGHT (faded/dashed for what we don't own), never the WORD 'care'. Two interactions carry the meaning: (1) click a hop → its payload + blast-radius; click a system → its subsystems (low-care ones behind '+N more'). (2) 'follow a value' chips — click one to light its path through every system; a value that never crosses an auth check lights the whole chain unbroken (that IS the finding). Dashed edge = leaves our trust domain; red edge = widens blast radius. REQUIRES elk.bundled.js on the page (vendored, offline): the renderer computes bands + ranks, ELK routes edges collision-free; falls back to a hand-rolled router if ELK is absent. Reach for this over io-boundary when the flow spans 3+ systems across 2+ trust domains and the COMPOSITION is the question.

techniques.when: understand execution order and what happens on a run
techniques.weak: static structure; comparing many values at once

techniques.when: compare two MODES of one structure (before/after, prod/test, sync/async)
let the reader choose depth; docs serving both skimmers and diggers
call ORDER and who-calls-whom; message-level differences; a value minted in one call and replayed in a later one by a different actor
techniques.note: Tag each lane with a trust domain (ours | caller | vendor) and mark every hop that LEAVES your domain. Drawing an intra-account hop and a vendor hop as identical arrows flattens the only boundary that matters. Pairs well with io-boundary: that view gives the surface, this one gives the order in which it is crossed.

techniques.when: 'what calls what' / call hierarchy; navigating a path like an outline
literate line-by-line walkthrough of real code; teaching a function
techniques.weak: architecture overview; flow across many files
techniques.note: PRIMITIVE: embed inside other techniques wherever code is shown

techniques.when: domains that ARE a state machine; transitions + trigger conditions
techniques.note: SIDE-CAR: rides alongside a step/flow view well

techniques.when: keep global context while reading local detail in a large change
build intuition for ORDER and causality by sweeping back/forth
techniques.note: often redundant with runtime-step; prefer step unless continuous scrubbing genuinely helps

techniques.when: depth-on-demand without EVER losing the whole
techniques.weak: precise A/B diff; printed/static output; simple linear reading

techniques.when: portable data-flow / control-flow that embeds in a PR, wiki, or ticket
techniques.weak: interactivity; deep per-node code; runtime state

techniques.when: portable call-sequence (who calls whom, in order) for a doc/PR
portable state machine for a doc/PR
classic node-edge DFD: sources, stores, processes, sinks; the 'good old' diagram

combined_examples.$comment: Composition patterns. See references/decision-rules.md for the when-to-combine rule. Golden reference lives in references/example-dryrun/catalog/combined-examples/.

A.name: Spine + Annotated Source
A.when: big-picture map that also lets you read the real code in place

B.name: Step-Through + State-Machine side-car
B.when: watch execution AND the state path it drives, together

C.name: Fisheye + Annotated + Minimap
C.when: deep-read one part while the whole stays on screen (never lose context)

D.name: Altitude + Annotated + Provenance
D.when: choose your depth, then read code AND trace values at the bottom

E.name: The Workbench
E.when: ANTI-PATTERN reference only: shows where integrated tips into cluttered; do not ship by default
